name: Coastwatchers Lighthouse
note: Landmark: working lighthouse on Madang harbour, a memorial to the WWII coastwatchers.

facts.text: A working lighthouse on Madang harbour that serves as the Coastwatchers Memorial.
The coastwatchers were mainly Australians who stayed in New Guinea after the Japanese invasion and, with local helpers, reported on Japanese ship and plane movements at great personal risk.

access_note: In Madang town; Wikivoyage says to avoid walking in town after dark.
unverified: Hours are not published; open-access memorial assumed

name: Madang Central Market
note: Market: busy local market in the centre of Madang, open daily, with produce brought in from the Highlands.

facts.text: A busy local market in the centre of Madang where people come from the Highlands with produce to sell.
Wikivoyage gives it as open every day except Sunday in one place and daily in another; it mainly sells fruit and vegetables, with a few bags, necklaces and t-shirts.
Buses to nearby towns leave from the central bus station next to the market.

access_note: In central Madang; avoid being out after dark.
unverified: Exact opening hours (Wikivoyage is internally inconsistent about Sunday)
Not a scheduled-hours source; no council page found

name: Krangket Island
note: Island: five-minute boat trip from Madang; two villages with gardens, a lagoon beach and a basic lodge.

facts.text: Krangket Island is a five-minute boat trip from the small boat terminal in Madang; boats leave every half hour and cost 2 kina.
Two villages with gardens and hedges, no roads, a lagoon beach and Krangket Lodge (two bungalows, 80 kina a night, bring your own food).

access_note: Short boat hop from Madang; the lodge is about half an hour's walk from the boat landing.

name: Karkar Island
note: Island: volcanic island 30 km off Madang with a caldera volcano (last big eruptions 1974-75), a ring road and views back to Madang; known for bilums.

facts.text: An oval volcanic island about 25 km by 19 km in the Bismarck Sea, with an active volcano having two nested calderas at its centre.
Eruptions in 1974-75 covered about 70% of the inner caldera floor; the 1979 eruption killed two volcanologists.
The island is known for the view from its mountain down to Madang town, and its fertile volcanic soil is farmed for food and cash crops.

access_note: Boat from Madang Province coast; no visitor facilities documented in sources found.

name: Lae War Cemetery
note: Cemetery: Commonwealth war cemetery with about 2,800 WWII burials, next to the botanic gardens and including the Lae Memorial.

facts.text: Contains 2,818 Commonwealth burials of the Second World War, 444 of them unidentified, per Wikivoyage; the Commission's own figure for identified casualties is lower.
Begun in 1944 by the Australian Army Graves Service and taken over by the Commission in 1947, beside the Lae Botanic Gardens; the Lae Memorial for Australians with no known grave stands inside.

access_note: In central Lae beside the botanic gardens; ordinary cautions for walking in Lae.

name: Rainforest Habitat
note: Wildlife: 10-hectare animal and bird display at Lae University of Technology, with about 80 birds of paradise in a rainforest enclosure.

facts.text: About 3,000 sq m of reconstructed rainforest inside a walk-through aviary under an 11 m canopy, with further enclosures, on the grounds of the PNG University of Technology.
Wikivoyage reports around 80 birds of paradise on display, from a dozen of PNG's 30 species.
Lonely Planet names a large saltwater crocodile as the star but reports collapsing walkways and derelict enclosures.
A Unitech PMV from Eriku drops at Gate No. 2, or it is a 15-minute walk from the main gate.
Run by Unitech Development & Consultancy; contact +675 473 4344.

access_note: About 9 km from central Lae; condition is reported as poor in the guide and may have changed.

name: Bulolo Gold Dredges
note: Relic: eight 2,000-tonne gold dredges airlifted into the Bulolo valley; some abandoned in the valley and still visible (Wikivoyage).

facts.text: Eight 2,000-tonne gold dredges were built for the Bulolo River; every part was airlifted into the valley using Junkers aircraft.

Dredging stopped in June 1965 after turning over 7.4 million cubic metres; one dredge was cut up to make bridges, two went to South America, and the rest in varying condition can still be seen abandoned in the jungle.
OSM maps two Gold Dredge attractions south-east of Bulolo town at about -7.248, 146.668.

access_note: Bulolo is a few hours' drive from Lae; no guide arrangement documented.
unverified: No hours, access conditions, fee or guide published

facts.fact: Active volcano reached by road; a parking lot where you pay, hot springs (deadly hot), views of ash deposits and volcano, and handicraft sellers; climbs start here
Tavurvur and Vulcan erupted on 19 September 1994 and covered most of Rabaul in ash
